A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReplaceMe study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM and CLIP pruning results, alongside calibration, solver, scaling, healing and multi-transform experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds layer-selection analyses, a compression-ratio comparison and task-specific calibration results.

M1.justification: Layer selection, least-squares/cosine estimation, the simplified cosine objective, MLP fusion, regularization and multiple transforms are retained. Expanded explanations of calibration averaging and fusion do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix A.17 adds SciQ training examples as a task-specific calibration source, expanding calibration-data coverage beyond the previously used sources. SciQ was already evaluated in v3; the evaluation benchmark suites and language/vision domains remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix A.10 adds CCA and CKA as empirically compared alternatives to the cosine layer-selection criterion in Figure 6. v3 compared cosine and L2 there. The principal pruning-baseline sets in the retained benchmark comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments specify SciQ training-split calibration with test-split evaluation and pairwise layer distances averaged over 256 SlimOrca samples. Table 3 adds an explicit 12.5%-50% compression comparison, although its model and healing configuration are unspecified. Existing training budgets and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v4 extends block-selection analysis with CCA/CKA comparisons and a layer-distance heatmap, adds the task-specific calibration ablation in A.17, and supplies additional compression-sensitivity evidence in Table 3. The extensive existing solver, regularization, masking, healing and multi-transform analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 retains the same repeated-experiment reporting: accuracy mean 60.71 with standard deviation 0.08, and perplexity mean 15.90 with standard deviation 0.05. Neither version specifies the run count there; v4 adds no new uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test.

E6.justification: Existing result tables retain their numerical values. New Table 3 reports, for example, average accuracy of 38.6 versus 30.4 for ReplaceMe and UIDL at 50% compression. Table 17 reports SciQ accuracy of 0.890 with task-specific calibration versus 0.858 with general calibration. A.10 also adds similarity curves and a heatmap; these are additional outcomes, not gains over matched v3 experiments.

T1.justification: The objectives, least-squares derivation, structured-transform solutions and mathematical definitions are retained. Changes from D to h and from cosine_distance to explicitly defined cos notation are equivalent notation changes, without new proofs or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free pruning, parameter-free fusion, competitive performance and applicability to language and vision transformers. The approximately 90% performance retention at up to 25% pruning claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds the interpretation that task-matched calibration improves target-task accuracy and discusses architecture-dependent pruning locations and natural layer grouping in A.10. Existing limitations concerning high compression and healing, and the accuracy/perplexity trade-offs, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 identifies CodeCarbon for environmental measurements and explicitly describes calibration averaging and reuse of calibration data. It supplies sampling and split details for the new analyses and corrects the configuration-table loss label from cosine similarity to cosine distance. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for CodeCarbon, CKA, CCA, earlier BERT compression work, DistilBERT and Transformer Layers as Painters. These support the added analyses and modestly broaden historical context; the central positioning against existing pruning approaches is retained.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v4 makes targeted explanatory and terminology edits, adds A.17, and updates author affiliations, equal-contribution information and the publication-status header.

P2.justification: The opening efficiency figure moves into the experiments and is redesigned into two panels with normalized time. v4 adds two analysis figures and two tables, revises captions and table emphasis, and replaces rotated model labels with horizontal group headings in the multi-transform table. Most existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional layer-selection checks and task-specific calibration experiment provide useful support beyond v3, while clearer calibration/fusion explanations and CodeCarbon disclosure improve assessability. These are limited gains: the main method, established results and uncertainty reporting remain stable, and the new high-compression table lacks explicit model and healing details.
